text: Given a request to any tool without X-Vercel-Access-Token, When the service handles it, Then it returns HTTP 401 with a body listing the required header(s), not a 500.

Given tools/list is called, Then all 19 tools are present and destructive tools (cancel/delete deployment, remove domain, delete dns record, delete env var) are annotated destructiveHint=true while read tools are annotated readOnlyHint=true.
Given a valid Vercel access token, When the agent calls vercel_list_projects, Then it returns the tenant's real Vercel projects (name, id, framework, latest production deployment).
steps: Obtain a real Vercel personal access token for a test account with at least one project
Call tools/call vercel_list_projects with X-Vercel-Access-Token set to that token
Inspect the returned project list
expect: Response contains the account's actual projects with name, id, framework, and latest production deployment fields; no error.
evidence: needs a real vendor account (no Vercel test account available during design/dev)

text: Given a project with multiple deployments, When the agent calls vercel_list_deployments with a limit, Then deployments are returned newest-first and capped at that limit.
steps: Call vercel_list_deployments for a project known to have more than 5 deployments, with limit=5
Check the order and count of the returned list
expect: Exactly 5 deployments returned, ordered newest-first by created time.

text: Given a project and a git ref, When the agent calls vercel_create_deployment, Then Vercel starts a new deployment and the tool returns its id, url, and initial state.
steps: Call vercel_create_deployment with a real project id and a valid git ref
Check the tool's response and cross-check in the Vercel dashboard
expect: Tool response includes a deployment id, url, and a state such as QUEUED or BUILDING; the deployment also appears in the Vercel dashboard.
evidence: needs a real vendor account; write operation, run on a disposable test project only

text: Given a deployment that is queued or building, When the agent calls vercel_cancel_deployment then calls it again on the same (now finished/canceled) deployment, Then the first call stops it and the second call returns a structured error, not a crash.
steps: Trigger a deployment and immediately call vercel_cancel_deployment on it
Call vercel_cancel_deployment again on the same deployment id
expect: First call reports a CANCELED state; second call returns the structured error envelope (invalid_argument or not_found), not a 500 or stack trace.

text: Given a project and a deployment id belonging to it, When the agent calls vercel_promote_deployment, Then production traffic points at that deployment and the tool confirms the new production deployment id.
steps: Call vercel_promote_deployment with a project id and an existing (non-current-production) deployment id
Check the project's production deployment in the Vercel dashboard
expect: Tool response confirms the new production deployment id; the Vercel dashboard shows the same deployment as production.
evidence: needs a real vendor account; run on a disposable test project only

text: Given a project, When the agent adds a domain, lists domains, removes the domain, and lists again, Then the domain appears then disappears; adding an already-attached domain returns a structured error.
steps: Call vercel_add_project_domain with a test domain
Call vercel_list_domains and confirm the domain is present
Call vercel_remove_project_domain for the same domain
Call vercel_list_domains again and confirm it is gone
Call vercel_add_project_domain again with a domain already attached to a different project
expect: Domain appears after add, disappears after remove; the duplicate-attach attempt returns a structured error, not a silent success.
evidence: needs a real vendor account and a test domain

text: Given a domain managed through this connector, When the agent creates a DNS record, lists records, then deletes it, Then the record appears then disappears in Vercel's DNS zone for that domain.
steps: Call vercel_create_dns_record for a test TXT or A record on a domain already attached via this connector
Call vercel_list_dns_records and confirm the record is present
Call vercel_delete_dns_record for that record id
Call vercel_list_dns_records again and confirm it is gone
expect: Record appears after create, disappears after delete.
evidence: needs a real vendor account and a test domain

text: Given a mocked Vercel response for the env-vars list endpoint that includes a value field, When vercel_list_env_vars processes it, Then the tool's output never contains a value key for any entry.
Given a project, When the agent creates an environment variable and then deletes it by id, Then the create response confirms id/name/targets without the value, and the delete removes it.
steps: Call vercel_create_env_var with name=TEST_VAR, value=some-secret, target=[preview]
Inspect the create response
Call vercel_list_env_vars and confirm TEST_VAR is present (no value field)
Call vercel_delete_env_var with the returned id
Call vercel_list_env_vars again and confirm TEST_VAR is gone
expect: Create response has id/name/targets, no value field anywhere; variable disappears after delete.
evidence: needs a real vendor account; use a disposable test project only, never a value that matters

text: Given two concurrent fake requests carrying different X-Vercel-Access-Token/X-Vercel-Team-Id header values, When each calls a tool, Then each outbound call to Vercel carries only its own request's header-derived token/team, never the other request's.

Given a request with only the access-token header vs. a request that also carries a team-id header, When each calls vercel_list_projects, Then the first operates on the token owner's personal account and the second operates on the named team only.
steps: Call vercel_list_projects with only X-Vercel-Access-Token (personal account token)
Call vercel_list_projects with the same or a different token plus X-Vercel-Team-Id set to a real team id
Compare the two project lists
expect: Personal-account call returns only personal projects; team-scoped call returns only that team's projects; no overlap/leak between the two beyond what is genuinely shared.

text: Given a mocked 404 response from Vercel for an unknown deployment id, When vercel_get_deployment or vercel_cancel_deployment is called, Then the tool returns the structured error envelope with code not_found, not a raw passthrough or an unhandled exception.

Given a mocked 429 response from Vercel with a Retry-After header, When a tool call hits it, Then the client retries with backoff honoring Retry-After and, once retries are exhausted, returns the structured error envelope with code rate_limited and retryable=true.
Given the service is running but egress to api.vercel.com is blocked, When GET /health is called without any credential header, Then it still returns 200 {"status":"ok"}.
steps: Start the service locally
Block or stub out egress to api.vercel.com (e.g. via a firewall rule or DNS override)
curl GET /health with no headers
expect: HTTP 200 with body {"status":"ok"}, returned without attempting to reach Vercel.
evidence: needs a local run (not a real Vercel account); deferred to dev leg's self-test
